b1_verification: AUDIT-2 B1 is FIXED. The round-2 diff against campaign/WP-43b/Surgery.lean.round1.bak touches only three things: (i) two new antecedents of IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy.rim, ContinuousOn tau_S (closedBall 0 R) and the shaft bound forall z, ||z|| <= R -> v + R/2 < tau_S z; (ii) the two new lemmas eqOn_closedBall_of_rim_antecedent and rimFun_eq_of_rim_antecedent, both 0 sorry; (iii) the two call sites (exists_spearSurgeryDatum, SpearSurgeryDatum.exists_shrink) and the docstrings. Under the new antecedent, (tau_S' z, z) lies in spear v R for ||z|| <= R, because fcoord = tau - r/2 > v. tau_S is therefore determined on the closed disc by S, and rimFun depends on S alone. I tried to re-derive False from SpearSurgeryDatum + IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy with five variants: (a) raising the vertex v' above sup tau_S, which is blocked (RimRegression proves it); (b) raising it within range, which gives tau_S' = tau_S and the same rim; (c) shrinking R' <= R, which gives the same tau_S restricted; (d) composing psi with an E0-automorphism (theta-rotation or tau-translation), which gives a reparametrised rim, C^1 iff the original is; (e) lowering the vertex, which needs spearY v'' R in W and is not supplied. None yields a contradiction. For an honest S that is C^1 spacelike on Reg M, rim holds: at r = R > 0 the null field d_tau is transverse to S, so S is a C^1 graph over z near the circle, equal to tau_S on it. The paper's hypothesis (B21 l.227: a smooth spacelike compact Cauchy surface) therefore implies IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy, so regM_isCauchyComplete_of_C1 is at least as strong as B21 Prop 2.17's first assertion, restricted to A = {0}. That restriction is disclosed as 'strengthened'.

(G2) Remark 2.12 is true given SurgeryData.isClosed and psi an open embedding on W. A component of an inextensible causal curve of Reg M in a closed spear has one of two past ends: a closed past end on the head (fcoord and r are non-decreasing along E0's Le, so it can enter neither through the shaft nor from the interior), where height = v + r/2 - G < 0 because G > v + R/2; or an open past end, where tau and r are monotone and bounded, z converges by Le.norm_sub_le (||dz|| <= 3 d tau), and the limit is either on the axis (second disjunct) or regular, which contradicts inextensibility. The future end is symmetric: exit through the shaft (rad = R), or tau unbounded. (G3) is true: Sigma* is closed in Reg M (the rims are in the cusps, and the cusps run to tau = +infinity at the axis); the past of a BTZ point is its line, so extensions in M of curves of Reg M add only BTZ-line pieces; S cap spear is an IsSpacelikeDiscGraph by acausality of S and continuity of tau_S; Cor 2.11 then matches the counts. (G5) is true: the compact part plus the cusps, which are complete on the strip, and the 2pi quotient of a complete length space is complete. (G1) is the paper's own construction (l.1091). Finiteness holds because S cap sing0 is compact and discrete (the line is causal and S acausal). Closedness and disjointness are asserted by B21 Def 2.1 / l.1091 and I found no counterexample. (G0) is plausible as stated after the repair; it is a cited smoothing theorem. issues.problem: The obstruction text overstates what is missing. It says 'no limit-extension lemma for flatCausality curves of Reg M is stated'. The strict library already has the general one: Causal.Causality.extensible_of_tendsto (Causal/Inextensible.lean:814; hypotheses: J^- closed, strongly causal, causally arc connected, causal, J^-(p) != {p}). It also has its corollaries Inextensible.not_tendsto_atBot / not_tendsto_atTop (Causal/Static.lean:962/989), inextensible_ordConnectedComponent (Causal/CauchyExtension.lean:688: the component of an inextensible curve in an open U is inextensible in U), and inextensible_iff_comp / inextensible_iff_invComp (CauchyExtension.lean:289/318, transport along an injective morphism). In lean-gx, E0.Le.norm_sub_le (BTZ/Causality.lean:2486: ||y.2 - x.2|| <= 3 (y.1 - x.1)) makes the coordinates of a monotone, tau-bounded arc converge, and E0Spear.le_of_isE0Mor (Spear.lean:408) moves the order into the chart. These cover most of steps (i)-(iii) of the text. The real residue is (a) the hypotheses of extensible_of_tendsto for flatCausality 2 (e0RegMFlat M), and (b) the identification flatCausality(Reg M) = CE(Reg M), which lives downstream in AbsMax.lean:954 (flatCausality_e0RegM_eq) and cannot be imported (cycle), so it must be re-proved or moved. The sorry is legitimate, but the stated obstruction is not precise.
